mail-kit

One email layer for every app. Never throws — it returns whether the mail was sent.

npm README & API Version history Source
OverviewAPI & examplesChangelogConsumersSources

Why it exists

Email is where products quietly grow a second, private implementation: a different sender, a swallowed error, a test message that reaches a real person. 23 apps had started.

How it works

Resend, over raw fetch, with no other dependencies. The call returns a result that says whether the mail went, rather than throwing and hoping a catch exists. Sandbox and placeholder addresses are refused, and the shared sender is one convention.

Where it fits

Hire, notifications, and anything that has to reach a person outside the product. It is the boring half of 'reach someone'. threadkit is the half that stays inside.

Read the package documentation

The fleet's one email layer. One env contract, one call shape, over Resend (the default) or the app's own mail server (SMTP). Zero runtime dependencies for Resend; SMTP uses nodemailer, an optional peer.

Exists because the fleet grew ~12 bespoke email implementations across three provider styles, and a dead SMTP credential silenced two apps' outbound mail for months without anyone noticing. Uniformity is the fix.

Install

pnpm add @bitbaum/mail-kit

Use

import { sendMail, isMailConfigured, mailHealth, conventionalFrom } from "@bitbaum/mail-kit";

const result = await sendMail({
  to: "person@example.ch",
  subject: "Your invoice",
  html: "<p>…</p>",
  attachments: [{ filename: "invoice.pdf", content: pdfBuffer, contentType: "application/pdf" }],
});

if (!result.sent) {
  // result.error, result.status?, result.retryable — sendMail NEVER throws.
  logger.error("invoice email failed", result);
}
  • sendMail never throws. A thrown email error inside a server action

reaches nobody and destroys the form; a { sent: false } you must look at is deliverable. Callers where delivery matters check .sent.

  • isMailConfigured() — gate flows that depend on an email arriving

(password reset, invoices). A placeholder key and a production sandbox sender (@resend.dev) count as unconfigured: both look configured and deliver to nobody.

  • mailHealth() — key-validity + domain-status probe for /api/health.

A passing probe does not prove delivery; only a real send does.

  • options.idempotencyKey — pass from crons/queues so a retried job

cannot double-send (Resend dedupes for 24h).

Resend or the app's own mail server

Resend is an HTTP email service: one API key, the fleet's shared verified domain. SMTP is the standard protocol for handing mail to a mail server, so an app that already sends through its own server keeps doing exactly that.

Resend stays the default. SMTP is chosen explicitly, never guessed from which variables happen to be set:

MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp
SMTP_HOST=mail.example.ch
SMTP_PORT=587          # default 587 (STARTTLS); 465 means implicit TLS
SMTP_SECURE=           # optional; defaults to true on 465, false otherwise
SMTP_USER=app@example.ch
SMTP_PASS=…            # USER and PASS together, or neither
SMTP_FROM="App <app@example.ch>"
pnpm add nodemailer    # only apps that choose SMTP

An app whose settings already live under other names passes them instead of renaming its env:

await sendMail(message, {
  transport: "smtp",
  smtp: { host: process.env.EMAIL_HOST!, port: Number(process.env.EMAIL_PORT), user: process.env.EMAIL_USER, pass: process.env.EMAIL_PASS },
});

The call, isMailConfigured, mailHealth and the result shape are the same for both. What differs, honestly:

  • Sender: SMTP reads SMTP_FROM, not RESEND_FROM — the shared Resend

domain is not your mail server's to send as. conventionalFrom() is a Resend convention.

  • Result: { sent: true, id } carries the SMTP Message-ID. A server that

accepts no recipient is sent: false. A 4xx reply or a dropped connection is retryable: true; a 5xx reply or a refused login is not. status is an HTTP status, so it is absent over SMTP; the reply code is in error.

  • idempotencyKey has no SMTP equivalent and is ignored there.
  • mailHealth() logs in without sending (no domain list).
  • Accepted is not delivered. A relay can answer 250 and drop mail from a

sender domain it has not authenticated. Check the sender domain's SPF/DKIM.

  • nodemailer missing → `{ sent: false, error: "SMTP transport needs the

nodemailer package…" }. The import carries webpackIgnore/turbopackIgnore`, so bundlers leave it to Node at send time instead of failing the build of a Resend-only app.

One layout for every email: renderMail

An app supplies a brand and content; the layout, dark mode, Outlook button, plain-text twin and footer rules live here, once.

import { renderMail, sendMail, listUnsubscribeHeaders, signUnsubscribe } from "@bitbaum/mail-kit";

const brand = { name: "Heidi", url: "https://heidi.orangecat.ch", accent: "#d9232d", onAccent: "#ffffff", accentDark: "#ff5a62" };

const { html, text } = renderMail(brand, {
  lang: "de-CH",
  preheader: "Kurz bevor Sie es vergessen würden: 8 Fragen, etwa 3 Minuten.",
  heading: "Heute sind **8 Fragen** fällig",
  blocks: [
    { type: "paragraph", text: "Drei Minuten jetzt, und sie bleiben ein paar Tage länger." },
    { type: "stats", items: [{ value: "8", label: "fällig" }, { value: "3", label: "Tage in Folge" }] },
    { type: "button", label: "Jetzt üben", url: "https://heidi.orangecat.ch/practice" },
  ],
  footer: {
    reason: "Sie bekommen das, weil Sie Erinnerungen eingeschaltet haben.",
    unsubscribe: { label: "Nicht mehr erinnern", url: unsubscribeUrl },
    preferences: { label: "Einstellungen", url: settingsUrl },
  },
});

await sendMail({ to, subject, html, text, headers: listUnsubscribeHeaders(unsubscribeUrl) });
  • Content is plain text. Every string is escaped; the only markup is **bold**. A link that is not http(s)/mailto throws.
  • Blocks: paragraph, button, link, code, stats, list, quote, note.
  • Dark mode follows the reader's client (prefers-color-scheme); give accentDark if your accent is too dark to read on black.
  • The footer is a required key. reason is always said. unsubscribe is {label, url} or null, and null is only for mail the person asked for this minute (a sign-in link).
  • System fonts, deliberately: webfonts fail in most mail clients.
  • Logo: brand.logoUrl must be a PNG (≥2× its shown 28px height); SVG does not render in Gmail or Outlook.

Unsubscribe that people do not hate

signUnsubscribe(secret, {user, list}) / verifyUnsubscribe make a signed, non-expiring token for a link that works without signing in. listUnsubscribeHeaders(url) adds List-Unsubscribe + List-Unsubscribe-Post: List-Unsubscribe=One-Click (RFC 8058), which Gmail and Yahoo require for bulk senders. The URL must act on a POST without a page, a login or a confirmation.

One address per app: hello@<host>

Every app has one address, on its own host, that a customer can guess: hello@<app>.orangecat.ch on the box, and hello@murphys-bar.ch once a site has its own domain. appAddress(url) builds it; appAddressFromEnv() reads MAIL_ADDRESS or derives it from APP_URL / NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL / AUTH_URL.

sendMail puts that address in Reply-To on every message (unless the call sets its own, or already sends from it). Mail still leaves through the shared sender until each host can sign its own — but every answer reaches the app.

Mail to an app

The fleet's mail gateway receives for every app host, checks SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and POSTs an InboundMail to /api/mail/inbound, signed with MAIL_INBOUND_SECRET (x-mail-signature: t=…,v1=hmac). The app side is one line:

// app/api/mail/inbound/route.ts
import { inboundHandler } from "@bitbaum/mail-kit";
export const POST = inboundHandler({ onMail: (mail) => saveAndTriage(mail) });

Unsigned, tampered, stale (> 5 min) or oversized deliveries are refused before your code runs; a thrown onMail answers 500 so the gateway retries.

AI triage

triageMail(mail, complete, context) asks a model (any complete() — the ai-forms / ai-kit shape) for kind, urgency, a one-line summary, the sender's language and needsHuman. It never throws: no model, or nonsense back, and the answer comes from plain rules, marked by: "rules". Instructions inside an email are described, never followed.

Env contract (the whole of it)

VarMeaning
`MAIL_TRANSPORT``resend` (default) or `smtp`
`RESEND_API_KEY`required to send through Resend (a fleet key: `/opt/fleet/env`)
`RESEND_FROM`sender — `Name <addr>` or bare address (optional if every call passes `from`)
`SMTP_HOST` …`SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_SECURE`, `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS`, `SMTP_FROM` — only with `MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp`
`MAIL_ADDRESS`the app's own address; optional, derived from the app's URL
`MAIL_INBOUND_SECRET`verifies mail from the gateway (a fleet key: `/opt/fleet/env`)

Fleet conventions

  • The shared Resend account is on the free tier: 1 verified domain,

100 emails/day, 3,000/month. Hitting the daily cap surfaces as { sent: false, status: 429, retryable: true }.

  • Only loki.orangecat.ch is verified, so every app sends as

<app>@fleetcrown.orangecat.ch — conventionalFrom("My App") builds it.

  • A daily canary on the box sends one real email and alerts Telegram when it

fails — that, not this package, is what proves delivery keeps working.

What this is not

  • Not a template engine — apps own their HTML.
  • Not a queue — retryable tells a caller whether a retry can help;

scheduling one is the caller's decision.

  • Not for bulk — newsletters go through Listmonk.

Changelog and releases

Read the repository changelog

This retrospective record was added on 2026-10-27 from the immutable sources linked below. Git commit dates are source dates, not inferred npm publication dates. A GitHub release does not itself establish npm publication. Application adoption and deployment evidence are tracked separately.

0.4.0

  • SMTP transport alongside Resend: MAIL_TRANSPORT=smtp (or { transport: "smtp" }) sends through the app's own mail server, configured by SMTP_HOST/SMTP_PORT/SMTP_SECURE/SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASS/SMTP_FROM or { smtp: {...} }. Resend stays the default; SMTP is never chosen implicitly.
  • nodemailer is an optional peer dependency, loaded only when SMTP is chosen. Resend-only apps install nothing new.
  • isMailConfigured, mailHealth and fromAddress are transport-aware; new mailTransport() and smtpConfigFrom().

0.3.0

  • renderMail(brand, content): one HTML layout for the fleet (extracted from OrangeCat's, made brandable) with dark mode, an Outlook button, a plain-text twin and a required footer. Content is plain text and escaped.
  • signUnsubscribe / verifyUnsubscribe / listUnsubscribeHeaders: signed one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058).
  • sendMail takes headers.
